question_text: Find the length of the chord intercepted by the circle x² + y² − 8x − 2y − 8 = 0 on the line x + y + 1 = 0.

insider_note: The whole answer rests on one right-angled triangle: radius as hypotenuse, perpendicular distance as one side, half the chord as the other — write 2√(r² − p²) as a formula line before substituting anything.

steps.label: Centre and radius
steps.margin_note: One mark. Halve the coefficients of x and y, then change the sign for the centre.
steps.memory_tip: Centre (−g, −f), radius √(g² + f² − c). The constant is subtracted, so a negative c makes the radius larger.
steps.why: The chord formula needs the radius and the distance of the line from the centre, so both centre and radius come first. Here c = −8, so −c is +8.

steps.label: Perpendicular distance from the centre
steps.margin_note: Second mark. Rationalise 6/√2 to 3√2 now — leaving the root in the denominator makes the next squaring harder to read.
steps.memory_tip: p = |ax₁ + by₁ + c| / √(a² + b²), with (x₁, y₁) the centre.
steps.why: The perpendicular from the centre to a chord bisects it, so its length is one side of the right-angled triangle whose hypotenuse is the radius.
common_mistakes: Using the coefficients of the circle instead of the line in √(a² + b²).
Leaving p as 6/√2 and then squaring it wrongly.

steps.label: Length of the chord
steps.margin_note: The last two marks. p² = (3√2)² = 18, not 6 — squaring a surd squares the number outside as well.
steps.memory_tip: Length of chord = 2√(r² − p²). Half the chord, the distance p and the radius r form a right triangle.
steps.why: The perpendicular from the centre bisects the chord, so half the chord is √(r² − p²) by Pythagoras, and the full chord is twice that. Since p = 3√2 < 5 = r, the line does cut the circle.

steps.label: The picture
steps.margin_note: No mark of its own; the question does not ask for a diagram. One rough sketch covers every chord question in this chapter.
steps.memory_tip: Radius, perpendicular distance and half the chord: a right-angled triangle every time.

elements.text: p is the distance from C to AB

steps.why: The perpendicular from the centre C to the chord AB meets it at its midpoint D. That makes triangle CDA right-angled at D with hypotenuse r, one side p and the other side half the chord — which is exactly the formula 2√(r² − p²).
common_mistakes: Drawing the perpendicular to a point other than the midpoint of the chord.
Taking the radius as the whole chord rather than as the hypotenuse.
